  "text": "Coda

The years went the way the tides went, by the table.

Maren's left hand stiffened first. It was the cold on the rail, the doctor in Bray said, and she said yes, it would be that. She wore the glove up the stair now and took it off only at the top, and the taking off was slow.

Erris Kessock was twenty-three and worked the boats. She was still on the wall most evenings. She no longer swung her heels.

"What time is it?"

"Ten to twelve."

One night in March, with the wind up and the harbour lying flat as a plate under it, Maren stopped at the lighthouse door and did not go in. She stood with her hand on the stuck wood and did not push.

Erris came up the low street behind her. She did not ask anything. She waited.

Maren took the key from her coat. It was warm. She held it out, and Erris took it, and that was all the ceremony there was.

"The eleventh step," Maren said. "Mind it."

She stood in the street and listened to the girl go up in the dark. She could not hear the clock from there. She had never been able to. She counted anyway, without meaning to, and then stopped counting.

At ten past, the water in the harbour moved the way water should move.

In the morning she opened the log and wrote the date and the time and the words wound, three turns, and under it, for the first time, another hand."
